newsitem.title: USA: US, EU meat talks to discuss new proposals - USDA.
newsitem.headline: US, EU meat talks to discuss new proposals - USDA.

text.p: U.S. and EU negotiators trying to resolve a fight over meat import regulations will resume meetings this week in Washington to discuss new proposals offered this past weekend, said Paul Drazek, senior trade advisor to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.

In an announcement released Tuesday, Drazek said USDA has notified the EU that the date on which Washington had planned to implement new meat and poultry inspection standards for EU plants exporting to the United States would be delayed to April 30 from April 15.

"As a result of discussions between U.S. and European Union negotiators over the weekend, during which several new proposals in the veterinary equivalency talks were discussed, it has been decided that EU negotiators will return to Washington later this week for further elaboration of those ideas," said Drazek.

"The U.S. Department of Agriculture has notified EU member countries and the EU Commission that the date on which we intend to implement our new policy regarding USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service verification of EU compliance with strict U.S. meat and poultry inspection standards will be April 30, 1997, rather than April 15."
The planned U.S. action could halt some $300 million worth of European meat products to the United States, mostly pork products from Denmark and Italian hams.

U.S. and EU negotiators have said that the biggest remaining obstacle towards reaching a settlement of the dispute has been disagreement over the U.S. poultry industry's use of chlorine in its decontamination process.
The U.S. poultry industry welcomed USDA's decision to delay its action, and said it is hopeful an agreement will be reached in the next two weeks.
